full_manifest_entry.title: Finite recursion and work accounting for multilevel MGRIT

citations.quote:
Input: levels $\ell=0,\ldots,L$ with $L\ge1$; fine-grid systems $A_\ell u_\ell=b_\ell$ of the form in [[def-linear-all-at-once-time-operator]]; coarsening factors $m_\ell\ge2$ dividing $N_\ell$ with $N_{\ell+1}=N_\ell/m_\ell$; transfers $P_\ell,R_\ell$ from the F/C construction in [[alg-mgrit-two-level-cycle]]; and pre/post-relaxations selected from its F- and FCF-relaxations. At each level $\ell<L$, form the practical coarse matrix $A_{\ell+1}$ with identity diagonal blocks and subdiagonal blocks $-\Psi_{\ell,j}$ as in [[alg-mgrit-two-level-cycle]]. Each noncoarsest level has a positive integer recursive visit count $\nu_\ell$. Also supply an initial fine-level iterate, a chosen norm on the fine-level residual space as in [[def-norm-and-normed-space]], outer cycle budget $J_{\rm out}\ge0$, and residual tolerance $\varepsilon\ge0$. The hierarchy must provide a nonsingular coarse system at every level and an exact solve on level $L$. V-cycles use $\nu_\ell=1$ and W-cycles use $\nu_\ell=2$. This algorithm gives no existence or convergence claim for a hierarchy that fails these input conditions.

For a recursive call at level $\ell$, perform the following operations on an initial guess $u_\ell$:
1. If $\ell=L$, solve $A_Lu_L=b_L$ exactly by forward substitution and return.
2. Apply the selected pre-relaxation to $A_\ell u_\ell=b_\ell$; compute $r_\ell=b_\ell-A_\ell u_\ell$ and restrict it to $r_{\ell+1}=R_\ell r_\ell$.
3. Set the coarse correction $z_{\ell+1}=0$. Repeat $\nu_\ell$ times: form $\rho_{\ell+1}=r_{\ell+1}-A_{\ell+1}z_{\ell+1}$; recursively apply the level $\ell+1$ cycle to $A_{\ell+1}\delta_{\ell+1}=\rho_{\ell+1}$ from zero initial correction; then set $z_{\ell+1}\leftarrow z_{\ell+1}+\delta_{\ell+1}$.
4. Correct $u_\ell\leftarrow u_\ell+P_\ell z_{\ell+1}$ and apply the selected post-relaxation.

Return the updated fine-level vector when the call completes. At level $0$, check the residual before the first outer cycle and after every completed cycle; return status converged only when the residual tolerance is met. After $J_{\rm out}$ cycles without a verified residual certificate, return the last iterate with status budget-exhausted. Inexact level solves contribute explicit update defects; no such defect is hidden in the exact-arithmetic cycle.

No two-grid contraction is transferred to this recursive cycle; convergence requires a bound for its actual full recursive error operator.

For the literal operations of [[alg-mgrit-two-level-cycle]], put $N_f=N$ and $N_c=N/m$. One F-relaxation uses $N_f-N_c-1$ fine-propagator calls; one C-relaxation uses $N_c$; and one FCF-relaxation uses $2(N_f-N_c-1)+N_c$. The specified coarse forward substitution uses $N_c$ practical coarse-propagator applications, including the evaluation at $z_0=0$. These counts concern completed operations without eliminating calls at zero inputs.

In an additive accounting model with nonnegative call costs $c_\Phi,c_\Psi$, the modeled work is $n_\Phi c_\Phi+n_\Psi c_\Psi+\kappa$, where $n_\Phi,n_\Psi$ count all executed calls and $\kappa$ accounts for all remaining work. Residuals, restriction, interpolation and stopping checks must contribute their actual calls and overhead; cached values incur no new call. A parallel schedule must respect the serial order within each F-interval and in the coarse solve, and its communication and synchronization. No measured speedup is asserted.

derivations.claim: A call on level $L$ terminates by the stipulated finite exact forward solve. If calls on level $\ell+1$ terminate, [F1] makes a finite number $\nu_\ell$ of them and otherwise executes only finite local operations, so a level $\ell$ call terminates. Downward induction proves termination on level $0$. There is one root call and every level $\ell$ visit has exactly $\nu_\ell$ children, giving the stated visit recurrence.

Each noncoarsest visit has its stated local work charge, and every coarsest visit costs $W_L$. Partition all operations by their unique executing visit and sum the charges to obtain $W$. At level $\ell$ the inherited relaxation has $N_f=N_\ell$ and $N_c=N_{\ell+1}$, so [F2] supplies its three call counts, including the boundary assignment without a call. The data dependencies in [F1] and in each relaxation/forward solve require the stated scheduling order. Summing actual visit charges also covers unequal costs, and outer checks are outside the recursive call.

full_manifest_entry.title: Propagator call counts for the two-level MGRIT cycle

citations.quote:
Input: a linear fine-grid system $A_tu=b$ with $N\ge1$ fine intervals as in [[def-linear-all-at-once-time-operator]], a coarsening factor $m\ge2$ dividing $N$ and its C/F partition as in [[lem-mgrit-exact-coarse-elimination]], practical coarse propagators $\Psi_j\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ for $1\le j\le N_c:=N/m$, an initial fine-grid iterate $u_{\rm in}$, pre- and post-relaxation choices from $\{F,FCF\}$, a real-valued norm on the fine-grid residual space as in [[def-norm-and-normed-space]], a nonnegative integer cycle budget $J_{\rm cyc}$, and a residual tolerance $\varepsilon\ge0$. The symbol $J_{\rm cyc}$ is the number of permitted cycles; the coarse-interval count is $N_c$ (the letter $J$ in [[lem-mgrit-exact-coarse-elimination]] denotes that lemma's coarse-interval count). The output is the last iterate, its residual norm, the number of completed cycles, and status `converged` or `budget-exhausted`.

In F/C ordering define ideal interpolation $P$ and restriction $R$ by
$$P=\begin{bmatrix}-A_{FF}^{-1}A_{FC}\\ I_C\end{bmatrix}, \qquad R=\begin{bmatrix}-A_{CF}A_{FF}^{-1}&I_C\end{bmatrix}.$$

The exact coarse operator is the Schur complement $RA_tP=A_{CC}-A_{CF}A_{FF}^{-1}A_{FC}$ from [[lem-mgrit-exact-coarse-elimination]]. The practical correction matrix $A_c$ has identity diagonal blocks and subdiagonal blocks $-\Psi_j$ for $2\le j\le N_c$; its first row corresponds to the fixed zero initial correction $z_0=0$. For any right-hand side $\rho$, forward substitution uniquely solves $A_cz=\rho$ by setting $z_0=0$ and, in increasing order for $j=1,\ldots,N_c$, setting $z_j=\rho_j+\Psi_jz_{j-1}$. Thus $A_c$ is invertible even when an individual $\Psi_j$ is singular.

Define the relaxations on $A_tu=b$ as follows. An F-relaxation holds every C-value fixed and, for each coarse interval $j=1,\ldots,N_c$, updates its F-indices $i=(j-1)m+1,\ldots,jm-1$ in increasing order: set $u_1=b_1$ if $i=1$, and otherwise set $u_i=b_i+\Phi_i u_{i-1}$. Different coarse intervals have independent F-updates and may be processed in parallel. A C-relaxation holds every F-value fixed and, for $j=1,\ldots,N_c$ in increasing order, sets $u_{jm}=b_{jm}+\Phi_{jm}u_{jm-1}$; these C-updates are independent because $m\ge2$ and each predecessor is an F-index. An FCF-relaxation applies F-relaxation, then C-relaxation, then F-relaxation. Each relaxation is a finite linear update; write $S_{\rm pre}$ and $S_{\rm post}$ for the error maps of the selected pre- and post-relaxations.

For one cycle from a current iterate $u$, apply the selected pre-relaxation; form $r=b-A_tu$ and $\rho=Rr$; solve $A_cz=\rho$ by the forward substitution above; correct $u\leftarrow u+Pz$; then apply the selected post-relaxation. The exact error-propagation matrix of this fixed cycle is
$$E=S_{\rm post}(I-PA_c^{-1}RA_t)S_{\rm pre}.$$

Initialize $u^{(0)}=u_{\rm in}$ and compute $\|b-A_tu^{(0)}\|$. If this is at most $\varepsilon$, return $u^{(0)}$, zero completed cycles, and status `converged`. Otherwise, for $j_{\rm cyc}=1,\ldots,J_{\rm cyc}$, perform one cycle, call the resulting iterate $u^{(j_{\rm cyc})}$, and compute $\|b-A_tu^{(j_{\rm cyc})}\|$. If this norm is at most $\varepsilon$, return that iterate, $j_{\rm cyc}$ completed cycles, and status `converged`; if not, continue. If all $J_{\rm cyc}$ cycles finish without this condition (including when $J_{\rm cyc}=0$), return the last iterate, its residual norm, and status `budget-exhausted`. The matrix $E$ describes exact arithmetic and exact coarse solves; inexact solves contribute an update defect that needs its own bound.

derivations.claim: There are $N_c$ C-indices among $N_f$ unknowns, leaving $N_f-N_c$ F-indices. Exactly the boundary assignment $u_1=b_1$ in [F1] omits a fine call, giving $N_f-N_c-1$ calls. Each of the $N_c$ C-updates makes one call. Adding two F counts and one C count gives the stated FCF count, including $N=m=2$, where the F count is zero.

The coarse loop in [F1] has $N_c$ iterations and executes one application per iteration, including $\Psi_1z_0$. Summing the stipulated charge for every executed call and remaining operation gives the work formula. Each F-index uses the preceding index in its interval, and the coarse loop uses $z_{j-1}$; any execution schedule must preserve these dependencies and account for its other costs.

full_manifest_entry.title: Work and idealized span of completed Parareal sweeps

citations.quote:
Input: an admissible propagator pair from [[def-parareal-propagator-pair]], initial state $x_0$, number of macro intervals $N$, integer sweep budget $K\ge0$, and optionally a wall-clock budget $\tau\ge0$ and certificate data $(\mathcal C,c,Q,V)$. Here $c\in\mathcal C$ is a supplied certificate, $Q$ is a declared predicate on completed rows, and $V(W,c)$ is a supplied deterministic verifier that terminates with a Boolean for every completed row $W$ and satisfies $V(W,c)=\mathrm{true}\Rightarrow Q(W)$. Without certificate data, take $V$ to return false. Every map call is required to terminate with a state or declared failure. Each map call either returns one state or a declared failure status. The output contains every fully completed row of the table $U_n^k$ for $0\le k\le K$, the last completed endpoint when one exists, and a status. If initialization never completes, return an empty completed-row table and no endpoint.

Initialize $U_0^0=x_0$ and, in increasing order of $n$, set $U_{n+1}^0=G_n(U_n^0)$. Store the values $G_n(U_n^0)$. For each $k=0,\ldots,K-1$, set $U_0^{k+1}=x_0$. Evaluate $F_n(U_n^k)$ independently for all $n$; the stored $G_n(U_n^k)$ values are reused from the preceding row. Then, in increasing order of $n$, compute $G_n(U_n^{k+1})$ and set
$$U_{n+1}^{k+1}=G_n(U_n^{k+1})+F_n(U_n^k)-G_n(U_n^k).$$
The fine calls in a sweep can run in parallel, while the corrected row is computed sequentially.

If a map call fails, return the last fully completed row and status propagation-failure; a prefix of the failed row may be reported separately but is not a completed iterate. If the time budget expires at a call boundary, return the last fully completed row and status budget-exhausted. When initialization and all $K$ requested sweeps finish, call $V$ on the final row and $c$ (or use false when no certificate was supplied). Return status converged if this returns true, certifying the declared predicate $Q$; otherwise return status budget-exhausted. Completion of the finite budget alone is not a convergence certificate.

For the exact-arithmetic recurrence, an update computed with inexact fine/coarse values or an inexact correction solve can be written as the displayed right-hand side plus a combined defect $\eta_n^{k+1}$. A residual tolerance alone does not bound that defect in forward error.

derivations.claim: Initialization makes $N$ coarse calls. Each of the $K$ sweeps in [F1] makes $N$ fine calls and $N$ new coarse calls, so the totals are $KN$ and $(K+1)N$. Multiplying by the stipulated costs and adding $K$ synchronization charges gives $W$.

Each fine phase has $N$ independent equal-cost calls and the prescribed batch schedule takes $\lceil N/P\rceil$ batches. Initialization takes $Nc_G$, and each sweep has this fine phase followed by $N$ serial coarse calls and one synchronization charge. Adding these sequential phases gives $S$, including $K=0$ and zero call costs.
